transcript: Thanks for being with us, I'm Rinse Green. State Senator, Leesburg resident, and Democrat Jennifer Wexton announced yesterday that she'll be going for a chance to run against Congressman Barbara Comstock next year. Wexton will have to first beat at least two other Democrats in the primaries, Dan Helmer. and Lindsey Davis Stover to run as a Democrat for Comstock's seat, representing the 10th District in Congress. Wexton has represented Virginia's 33rd Senate District since 2014 when she won a special election to replace Mark Herring, who had just been elected Attorney General. Mark Herring, by the way, former member of our Board of Supervisors. Wexton criticized Comstock for voting in line with Republicans and President Donald Trump and for refusing to hold an in-person town hall, which has been a hot-button issue with Indivisible and other resistance groups in the 10th District. Wexton said she has held four town halls since February. Go to LoudonOut.com slash Morning Minute to check out the whole story. In other news, a mysterious substance found that an envelope evacuated a county government building yesterday. Three staffers in the Shenandoah building, which is on heritage way near the Walmart in Leesburg, called 911 yesterday afternoon after they found the envelope. The building was evacuated, and the people who found the envelope were rinsed off and quarantined. Hazmet technicians suited up and went into the building to identify the substance. Happily, it was found not to be hazardous, and the fire department gave the all clear. 100 women strong announced $194,000 in donations to 20 Loudon Nonprofits Tuesday. Since 2008, they've donated more than $1.3 million to Loudon Nonprofits. They also support two long-term projects, the Community School Initiative at Sterling Elementary and the Loudon County Public Schools Backpack Coalition. Read the full list of grantees and what school superintendent Eric Williams showed up to tell them about full-day kindergarten over at LoudonNow.com. Loudon Motorsports in Leesburg is closing down after 20 years in business. They're selling their building on Catoctin Circle to Ketterman's Jewelers. Greg and Elizabeth Voll started Loudon Motorsports in June of 1997. They were in their early 30s and looking for something different from their careers as an attorney and a sports marketing executive they told us. They say they may go try their hands at farming. Over on their 30 acre property near Hamilton. Speaking of closing, the One Loud and Fresh Mart is also closing down. They haven't announced a specific closing date yet. The nearest fresh markets are on Winchester and Vienna. The One At One Loud has been there since November of 2013. The town planning and zoning department says it will be gathering public input on the project, probably on the town website hasn't been launched yet though. Get the full stories at loudnow.com. While you're there, read about Tammy Umbel, the homeschooling mom of 14 and founder and CEO of a nationally distributed line of natural body care products. Also, check out the story about the non-profit equine therapy group that brings healing to both horses and people. They name a horse as one of their co-founders as a matter of fact. While you're there, sign up for our daily newsletter. On today's calendar, see an exhibition of the work of painter Andre Potter at the National Sporting Library and Museum in Middleburg, opening today and running through August 13th. Catch Nathaniel Davis live at Brew Loco and lands down at 6 p.m. Stop by Jack's Run Brewing Company in Percival for open mic night with Victor Torres at 6.30 p.m. and check out Alex Young live at Trinity House Cafe in Leesburg at 7 p.m. Check out the rest of the events calendar at loudandnow.com slash events. And keep in mind, by the way, the Leesburg streets close down at 5 to get ready for flowering garden this weekend. And stop on by and see us at our tent. We'll be over on King Street. Okay, have a great day!
